doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Talking saxophones: Selmer, King and Rowe's Buffet
summary: They compare their horns, his Selmer VI and a King Super 20, and Rowe's old Buffet with its patina.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I should send you the transcript of what you said back then because, like today, you’re very quotable, Charles. So I want to wrap up just a little bit of talk, I rarely do this but —
Okay.
Talk about saxophones.
Okay.
Because when I saw the video from Smoke I thought your saxophone, your alto was quite experienced-looking.
Oh that’s true. It’s an old Selmer.
It was a beautiful thing. Can you just hold it up there?
Now wait a minute because was it the record date because I played at Smokes twice, the record date it was on a Selmer VI and then I appeared at Smoke, maybe a year later, and it was a King Super 20.
Well I’m not sure which horn it was.
If I see the picture I’ll know which one it was.
Yes, but which one do you have with you now?
I have the Selmer. Want me to play a couple of notes on it?
Well I’d love to compare the —
Oh okay, now let me see your horn, let me see your neck.
This is a Buffet.
Oh that’s a Buffet?
Yes. And —
Wow. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
The reason I was doing this is because I noticed something in your horn, whichever it was, and that was you know for years people have looked at this horn and go, “Wow, that’s old.”
Yeah. It’s an old —
Finally somebody said, “Oh what a nice patina.” Patina. So that’s the word I’ve latched on to, to make me feel good about my horn.
Patina. Yeah. Well you know when I saw the neck I thought it was a Selmer Balance Action.
Okay.
Well yeah. But those — I did have a Buffet at one time but I had a newer one. Yours is older than mine and I bet money that the sound is beautiful on that.
Yeah. I’ve had it since 1966.
You want to play it for me?
No not really.
All right. Okay.
Well this has been fascinating, Charles, you’re a very deep thinker. And you can come up with better adjectives than I can.
Oh I don’t know about that.
